extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent prosecutors and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for patent examiners on rejections and related prosecution matters (new matter, foreign filing, disclaimer, res judicata, reissue, previously-allowed claims, and final rejection practice), including form paragraphs and statutory citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and objecting to new matter (35 U.S.C. 132(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examination of an application following amendment thereof, the examiner must be on the alert to detect new matter. 35 U.S.C. 132(a) should be employed as a basis for objection to amendments to the abstract, specification, or drawings attempting to add new disclosure to that originally disclosed on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is added to the specification, it should be objected to by using Form Paragraph 7.28. If new matter is added to the claims, or affects the claims, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, using form paragraph 7.31.01 should also be made. If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed and it is not shown in the drawing, the claim is not rejected but applicant is required to add it to the drawing (see MPEP § 608.01(l)). Examiner should identify new matter by page and line numbers/drawing figures and provide an explanation addressing applicant's support arguments and any unresolved questions about possession at time of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.28 — Objection to New Matter Added to Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Template objection: 'The amendment filed [1] is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132(a) because it introduces new matter into the disclosure... The added material which is not supported by the original disclosure is as follows: [2]. Applicant is required to cancel the new matter in the reply to this Office action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is not to be used in reissue applications (use form paragraph 14.22.01 instead). In bracket 2, identify the new matter by page and line numbers and/or drawing figures and provide an appropriate explanation of your position. The explanation should address any applicant statement supporting possession at filing and include any unresolved questions raising doubt. If new matter affects claims, also make a 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph rejection (form paragraph 7.31.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require adding omitted illustrative subject matter to drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed and it is not shown in the drawing, the claim is not rejected but applicant is required to add it to the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(l) for procedure; do not reject the claim solely for missing drawing illustration—require drawing amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for unauthorized disclosure / Foreign filing without license (35 U.S.C. 182)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention disclosed in an application for patent subject to an order made pursuant to section 181 may be held abandoned upon establishment that in violation of said order the invention has been published or disclosed or that an application has been filed in a foreign country by the inventor or persons in privity without consent of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment is deemed to have occurred as of the time of violation. A holding of abandonment constitutes forfeiture of all claims against the United States based upon such invention. Examiner must be aware of orders under section 181 when foreign disclosures or filings are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing in foreign country without license (35 U.S.C. 184) — six-month rule and license scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when authorized by a license obtained from the Commissioner, a person shall not file in any foreign country prior to six months after filing in the United States an application for patent or for registration of certain IP rights in respect of an invention made in this country. The term 'application' includes modifications, amendments, supplements, or divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license may be granted retroactively where an application has been filed abroad through error and without deceptive intent and the application does not disclose an invention within the scope of section 181. The scope of a license shall permit subsequent modifications, amendments, and supplements containing additional subject matter if the original U.S. application was not required to be made available for inspection under section 181 and such modifications do not change the general nature of the invention so as to require inspection under section 181. If a license is not required to file abroad, subsequent modifications may be made without a license to the foreign application if the U.S. application was not required to be made available under section 181 and modifications do not change the general nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent barred for filing abroad without license (35 U.S.C. 185)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person shall not receive a United States patent for an invention if that person or related parties, without procuring the license prescribed in section 184, have filed an application in a foreign country for a patent or registration of certain IP rights in respect of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A U.S. patent issued to such a person shall be invalid unless the failure to procure the license was through error and without deceptive intent, and the patent does not disclose subject matter within the scope of section 181. Examiner should consider these conditions when assessing patentability/validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when corresponding foreign application exists (possible violation of §184/185)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner learns of a corresponding foreign application which appears to have been filed before the U.S. application had been on file for six months, and the invention apparently was made in this country, he or she shall refer the application to Licensing and Review Section of Technology Center work group 3640, calling attention to the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending investigation the application may be returned to the TC for prosecution on the merits. When otherwise in condition for allowance, the application will again be submitted to Licensing and Review Section unless they report no bar. If action under 35 U.S.C. 185 is necessary, Licensing and Review Section will request transfer of the application to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer rejection grounds (applicant-disclaimed subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter involved. Such disclaimer may arise from, for example: (A) failure to make claims suggested for interference, (B) failure to copy a claim from a patent when suggested by the examiner, or (C) failure to respond or appeal within time to examiner's rejection of claims copied from a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from the disclaimed subject matter as well as to the claims directly involved. Rejections based on disclaimer should be made using one of Form Paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.48 — Failure To Present Claims for Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Template rejection: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based upon claim [3] of Patent No. [4]. Failure to present claims and/or take necessary steps for interference purposes after notification ... constitutes a disclaimer of the subject matter.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph only after applicant has been notified that interference proceedings must be instituted and applicant has refused to copy the claims. In bracket 2 insert --102(g)-- or --102(g)/103(a)--. In bracket 4 insert the patent number, and --in view of _____-- if another reference is also relied upon. When rejection under 103(a), include basis for obviousness. Note interferences may include obvious variants (see MPEP Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.49 — Rejection, Disclaimer, Failure To Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Template rejection: 'An adverse judgment against claim [1] has been entered by the Board. Claim [2] stand(s) finally disposed of for failure to reply to or appeal from the examiner’s rejection...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse judgment against a claim is a final action of the Office requiring no further action to dispose of the claim permanently. See 37 CFR 41.127(a)(2). Use when claims are finally disposed by Board judgment or failure to appeal as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata as a ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may constitute a proper ground for rejection but should be applied only when the earlier decision was by the Board of Appeals or a reviewing court and when there is no opportunity for further court review of the earlier decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Court has materially restricted res judicata rejections, apply with care. Ordinarily also take action on the basis of prior art, especially in continuing applications. The same prior art relied on earlier would often be applicable. The MPEP lists cases where such rejections were sustained and where they were reversed—consider differences in claims, new evidence, or other procedural issues when deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application limitations (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids granting a reissue 'enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent' unless the reissue is applied for within 2 years from the grant of the original patent. This prohibition applies to any claim broader in any respect than the original patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims broader in any respect may be rejected as barred by 35 U.S.C. 251. However the statute permits reissue by assignee only where it does not enlarge the scope. A defective reissue oath is a ground for rejecting all claims in the reissue application (see MPEP §1444). Note a reissue application is 'special' and remains so even if applicant does not make a prompt reply. See MPEP Chapter 1400 for reissue examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of previously-allowed claims — examiner caution and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection has been submitted to the primary examiner for consideration of all the facts and approval of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised in authorizing such a rejection. Full faith and credit should be given to the search and action of a previous examiner unless there is clear error or knowledge of other prior art. In general, an examiner should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely in hope of finding something. Because unusual to reject previously allowed claim, point out in office action that the claim was previously allowed by using Form Paragraph 7.50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.50 — Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected, New Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Template paragraph: 'The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) to [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the name(s) of the newly discovered reference. Any action including this form paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner (see MPEP §1004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection practice — when a rejection may be made final (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final, whereupon applicant’s reply is limited to appeal or to amendment as specified. Reply must comply with §1.114 or paragraph (c). (b) In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims, clearly stating the reasons in support thereof. (c) Reply must include cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before final rejection, develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant where possible. Claims should be thoroughly searched and references fully applied in the first action where possible. Avoid hasty final rejections. If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection, the final may refer to it but should include rebuttal of applicant arguments. The applicant is entitled to a full and fair hearing; prosecution should be confined to as few actions as consistent with thorough consideration. Use Form Paragraph 7.39 to conclude final rejection letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.39 — 'Action Is Final' (content & timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template concluding paragraph for final action informing applicant the action is made final and reminding of extension-of-time policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a). It specifies a shortened statutory period for reply (THREE MONTHS) and conditions related to advisory action timing and maximum statutory period (SIX MONTHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This form paragraph should not be used in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings where 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not available. Form paragraph 7.39.01 may be used to notify applicant of options available after final rejection. The Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 should be used in all Office actions up to and including final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.39.01 — Final Rejection, Options for Applicant, Pro Se
rubrics_metrics.description: Template paragraph explaining options after final rejection: appeal to Board (Notice of Appeal within reply period with fee) or attempt amendment (entry of proposed amendment after final is not a matter of right unless it merely cancels claims or complies with a formal requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to file an amendment after final, admission is discretionary and may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not presented earlier. Filing an amendment after final does not stop the running of the statutory period for reply unless examiner holds the claims in condition for allowance. If a Notice of Appeal is not properly filed within the period for reply (or extension obtained), the application will become abandoned. The form paragraph must be preceded by one of specified form paragraphs (7.39, 7.40, etc.). See MPEP §§714.12, 714.13 for amendments after final.

rubrics_metrics.name: When final rejection is proper on second or subsequent action and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under present practice, second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the required fee. Where information is submitted in an IDS with the fee, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final whether or not claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection not necessitated by amendment is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second or subsequent action should not be made final if it includes a rejection on prior art not of record of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed. If applicant files a statement averring common ownership disqualifying a 102(e) reference, the examiner may not make the next action final if a new rejection is made. Note special rules for reexaminations. See MPEP §706.07(a) and §609.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejections in continuing/substitute applications and RCEs (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if entered in the earlier application. Claims in an RCE may be finally rejected in the action immediately subsequent to filing the RCE where similar conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A first action in a continuing or substitute application or an RCE may not be made final if it contains a new ground of rejection necessitated by amendments to 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (per the 2002 amendments). It is improper to make final a first action where the application contains material presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but denied entry for reasons such as new issues or new matter questions (e.g., continuation-in-part with new subject matter). A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted. Use Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs 7.40 / 7.40.01 / 7.40.02 — Actions made final necessitated by amendment, IDS with fee, or joint research agreement exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.40: 'Applicant’s amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' ¶7.40.01: similar wording when IDS filed under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee prompted the new ground(s) of rejection. ¶7.40.02: similar wording when submission invoking joint research agreement prior art exclusion under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) prompted the new double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph reminds applicant of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy and the shortened statutory period for reply (three months, with described conditions). Examiner Notes: these form paragraphs should not be used in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings where 1.136(a) is not available; do not use where other new grounds not necessitated by amendment or IDS with fee are introduced. For 7.40.01 and 7.40.02, bracket instructions require insertion of filing dates of the IDS or joint-research requirements respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.41 — Action Is Final, First Action (continuation/substitute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template paragraph: 'This is a [1] of applicant’s earlier Application No. [2]. All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action in this case.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert either --continuation-- or --substitute-- in bracket 1 and the earlier application number in bracket 2. Remind applicant of extension policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and the shortened statutory period. Use when first-action-final conditions described in MPEP §706.07(b) are met.
